set.title: Top tabs: one row that side-scrolls everywhere, sticky under a header that scrolls away; half the side padding on mobile
set.expected: The owner (2026-10-24, prompt log ai/2026/10/20/session-e00f55c9/page.jsonl lines 404 and 406). Step 1 landed as a quick fix: ai/rail/rail.css, merge 2865590d4 (the AI tab bar side-scrolls on mobile). Now: (1) the same tab rows are everywhere (the ext/Doc module tabs too): one row, side-scroll, never wrap. (2) Make the tab row a sticky header. The framework header (with the hamburger) should scroll away normally, and the tabs should stick at the top. If a scrollable tab strip blocks that, try it, and drop it if it needs fragile JS. (3) On mobile, halve the left and right padding: the tabs pad, and the white cards inside pad again. Check whether the standard padding token is used, weigh a 'slim' modifier against pages simply getting less side padding on phones, pick one and say why. Shots at 390 and 1920, scrolled and unscrolled. Land ready to merge.

log.msg: Survey of top tab rows: (1) ext/tabs/tabs.css .tab-bar is the shared rule and is already nowrap + overflow:auto. (2) ext/Doc/Doc.css .page.doc-page > .tabs > .tab-bar overrides to flex-wrap:wrap + overflow:visible above 600px (module tabs, 2026-09-29), nowrap+scroll at <=600px. (3) ai/rail/rail.css .page--ai .inbox-head > .tabs > .tab-bar side-scrolls only <40em (qf-2). All three are the same shared .tab-bar. Scroll model at <=52em: topic is a column [sticky .sidebar header][.pages overflow-y:scroll]; the header is a SIBLING above the scroller so it can never scroll away unless the topic becomes the scroller. Sticky inside AI is capped by its parent .inbox-head (73px tall).

Decision (sticky): keep it CSS-only. A new word .tabs.stick (ext/tabs/tabs.css, one rule) pins the strip; Doc.js and ai/page.js add it. Sidebar.css <=52em: when a topic holds a .tabs.stick, the TOPIC becomes the scroller (overflow:auto), the header goes position:relative (still the anchor of the open menu) so it scrolls away, and .pages stops scrolling (flex:1 0 auto, overflow:visible). Proven by CSS injection at 390: header gone, tabs stuck at y=0 on /core/Page/ and /ai/queue/. AI needs .inbox-head display:contents <40em because sticky is capped by its parent (73px). Other top rows (ai2/page.js, ux/Browse, ux/Inbox demo) are .inbox-head full/fill apps with an inner scroll: their head never scrolls, so they only need the shared side-scroll, no stick.

Found while verifying: ux/Inbox/Inbox.css had its own wrapping tab row and opaque-less --well fill on .inbox-head > .tabs > .tab-bar, which beat the shared rule and kept the AI queue row two lines at 390. Fixed there (commit 3692d182c): dropped flex-wrap, and the background now applies only to .tabs:not(.stick). Tab rows changed: ext/tabs .tab-bar (shared), ext/Doc doc-page bar (wrap override removed), ai head (ai/page.js now block stick + rail.css), ux/Inbox head (shared by ai2, Browse, Inbox demo: side-scroll only, not sticky).

Part 3 decision: lowered the .page --gutter-x floor from clamp(2em,4%,5em) to clamp(1em,4%,5em) (Page.css, restated in ext/Doc/Doc.css), about 28px -> 15.6px a side at 390, no change from ~700px up. Chose every-page-at-the-source over a per-page slim word: the rule is one token, it halves every page with no opt-in to forget, and a slim word would need adopting on hundreds of pages. Left --pad-card (white cards, floor 1rem) alone: its floor was fitted on purpose for narrow cards at every width, and with the gutter halved the card text sits about 32px in at 390, from about 44 before. Queue already used its own 16px gutter, so only its card spacing is unchanged.

ready: worktree/top-tabs at d263d6683 (3 commits + readmes). TAB ROWS: shared ext/tabs .tab-bar (nowrap + overflow auto, overscroll contained); ext/Doc doc-page bar and ai head and ux/Inbox head no longer wrap (ux/Inbox is shared by ai2, Browse, Inbox demo: side-scroll only, not sticky). STICKY: yes, CSS-only, opt-in .tabs.stick in ext/tabs (Doc.js and ai/page.js add it); on a phone styles.css (<=52em) makes the topic the scroller so the header scrolls away; wide screens stick to the page scroll (AI queue at 1920 scrolls inside, its head is already fixed). PADDING: .page --gutter-x floor 2em->1em at the source (Page.css + Doc.css), ~28px->15.6px a side at 390; --pad-card left alone. decision.question: review size
decision.why: sitewide: every tab row side-scrolls; .tabs.stick + page-as-scroller on phones (styles.css); .page side padding floor 2em to 1em in Page.css and Doc.css

findings.text: On a wide screen the stuck tab strip doesn't cover the full width. The strip sits beside the title (`flex: 1 1 24em`), so when the title scrolls away, the content scrolls through the empty spot to its left: the properties card shows at the top-left in shots/page-1920-scrolled.png (x 310–460, y 0–77), and so does the dark code block in shots/tabs-1920-scrolled.png. Ask 2, "on a wide screen, the tab row sticks", is only half met.

The code block on core/Page now runs to the right screen edge at 390 (shots/page-390-top.png, band 6, x 16–390), and so does the page.jsonl block in shots/page-390-scrolled.png. In shots/before-page-390-top.png it stopped 28px short. The smaller `--gutter-x` probably dropped the right inset of the wide blocks. (layout 5, spacing)

The page title and the content no longer share a left edge on a phone. "Task queue" starts at about x 8, but its cards start at x 16 (shots/queue-390-top.png, bands 3–4). On /framework/ai/ at 400, layout.json `left_stack.h1` is 12, while the content starts at 24. (layout, one left edge)
At 1920 the AI queue page is too short to scroll, so shots/queue-1920-scrolled.png looks the same as -top. Nothing shows the AI tab strip sticking on a wide screen.

On /framework/ai/ at 400, the filter chips (Ready to merge … Processes) wrap onto 3 rows (shots/…-framework-ai/400.png, band 2). They are a chip row, not a `.tab-bar` (layout.json `tab_rows` 0), so the brief's "every tab row" may not cover them. Still, they read as tabs and take 3 lines.

answer.reply: noted: at 1920 the AI page is a full-height app with its own inner scroll, so its head never moves and has nothing to stick to. The wide-screen sticky is shown on the ext/Doc pages instead (page-1920-scrolled, tabs-1920-scrolled), and R1 fixes the gap there.
noted: that is the AIDashboard filter-chip row, not a tab row. The AI dashboard task (ai-dashboard, next) rebuilds the top of /framework/ai/, and this finding was added to its brief (part 1).

log.msg: fix round 1, R1: the Doc strip's gap left of the stuck strip is closed. Chosen: paint the stuck .tab-bar outward (an outset box-shadow in --well over the ground, plus clip-path: inset(0 0 0 -100vw) so it spreads leftward only) in ext/tabs tabs.css, commit 4c6dbad5d. Why not a second row or moving the title: nothing moves in the layout, the strip keeps sharing the title's line, and the .pages scroller clips the paint so it never reaches the sidebar. Proof: shots page-1920-scrolled.png and tabs-1920-scrolled.png now show one unbroken band above the content (x 310-460, y 0-77 painted).

fix round 1, R2: not a bug, no change. Measured at 390 on /framework/core/Page/: the .code-block rect is x 15.6 to 374.4 (16px left, 15.6px right), and a pixel scan of page-390-top.png rows 640 and 690 reads dark at x 16 and background (242) from x 374. The section's padding-right is 15.59 = --gutter-x, so the blocks follow the gutter and nothing is tuned to the old 2em.

fix round 1, R3: not caused by this task (before-queue-390-top.png has h1 at x 8, cards at 16). Cause: a second inset. The page already pays --gutter-x (8.4px) and .tq-view added padding 0 clamp(0.5em,2cqi,1.2em) (7.8px) on top, while the h1 sits outside it. Fixed with one declaration: .tq-view padding 0 0 2em (ai/queue/TaskQueueView.css, 0e7ccf1bb); h1 and cards now both start at 8.4 at 390 and share x 280 at 1920. Same pattern on the AI dashboard at 400 (h1 12, content 24): .ad-dash padding 0.8em clamp(0.6em,3cqi,1.5em) 2em became 0.8em 0 2em (ai/AIDashboard/AIDashboard.css, 3f59783aa); both start at 12. Re-checked leak: stick-leak.mjs gives auto/relative on the queue and visible/sticky on /framework/ and Chat. Shots regenerated.
